subject: biology
title: Light and electron microscopes
key_idea: Light microscopes are affordable and can show living cells, but their magnification and resolution are limited. Electron microscopes have much higher magnification and resolution. They show sub-cellular structures in fine detail, which has helped biologists understand many more structures inside cells.

blocks.text: A light microscope uses light and lenses to magnify a specimen. This section covers what it can and cannot show.

items.meaning: How many times bigger the image is than the real object.
The ability to tell two objects that are close together apart. Higher resolution shows more detail.
A dye that makes colourless structures in a cell easier to see.

items: Affordable, easy to use and portable.
Can show living cells, and shows colour.
Has a large field of view.
Lower magnification and resolution, so small sub-cellular structures cannot be seen clearly.
Use a **thin layer** of cells so that light can pass through.
Add a **stain** such as iodine to see the parts of the cell.
Lower the cover slip at an angle to reduce air bubbles.

blocks.label: Total magnification
blocks.formula: total magnification = eyepiece lens magnification × objective lens magnification
where: Both lenses are given as ×, for example ×10 or ×40.

items: Light microscopes show living cells, in colour, and are cheap and easy to use.
Stains make colourless structures visible.
Total magnification is the eyepiece magnification multiplied by the objective magnification.

blocks.text: An electron microscope uses a beam of electrons instead of light. Electrons have a shorter wavelength than light.

items: Much **higher magnification** than a light microscope.
Much **higher resolution** (resolving power), so smaller structures can be seen.
Light microscopes resolve about 0.2 µm. Electron microscopes resolve about 0.0001 µm (0.1 nm).
Some electron microscopes give a 3D image.
Expensive and not portable.
Specimens must be very thin sections and cannot be living.
Preparation takes longer and is more complex.
Images are black and white.
Electron microscopes have higher magnification and higher resolution.
Greater resolution means smaller structures can be seen in detail.
They are expensive, and the specimen cannot be living.

blocks.text: Microscope technology has developed over time. Each improvement lets biologists collect new evidence.

items: Many sub-cellular structures were not clearly visible until electron microscopy.
Electron microscopes show structures such as mitochondria and ribosomes in fine detail.
Viruses are too small to see with a light microscope. An electron microscope is needed.
New technology gives new evidence, so scientific ideas change to fit it.

checks.q: Give two advantages of an electron microscope over a light microscope.
checks.a: Higher magnification and higher resolution (it can show smaller sub-cellular structures in more detail).

checks.q: A student uses a ×10 eyepiece and a ×40 objective lens. Calculate the total magnification.
Explain why a stain is added to a specimen for a light microscope.
checks.a: Cell structures are colourless. The stain makes them easier to see, so the parts of the cell can be seen.

worked_example.question: Give two advantages of using an electron microscope instead of a light microscope.
answer_points: Higher resolution or resolving power (it shows more detail, or smaller sub-cellular structures).
worked_example.tip: One mark for each. "Bigger" and "zoom" are ignored here.

worked_example.question: Explain why using an electron microscope shows the structures in the white blood cells more clearly.
answer_points: So smaller structures can be seen or identified.
Electrons, with a shorter wavelength, are used instead of light.
worked_example.tip: Any two score one mark each. Link resolution to what can be seen.

worked_example.question: Transmission electron microscopes (TEM) work by passing a beam of electrons through a very thin slice of an object. Suggest one advantage and one disadvantage of using TEM rather than a light microscope to look at cells.
answer_points: Advantage: increased resolution, or high magnification, or sub-cellular structures are visible.
Disadvantage: can only be used on dead material, or thin sections only, or gives a 2-D image, or expensive, or preparation takes longer, or black and white images.
worked_example.tip: One mark for an advantage and one for a disadvantage. "Clearer" or "can see small cells" is ignored.
